newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares enjoy pre-budget rally.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares enjoy pre-budget rally.

text.p: Singapore shares enjoyed a pre-budget rally at midday on Monday, dealers said.

"The market is expecting Friday's budget to be pro-business and that has helped lift investors' mood," said a dealer with a local trading house. "Positive media reports that now is a good time to buy is also helpful."
He said foreign tranches of banks like DBS, UOB and OCBC were among the first few stocks to be bought as they stood to benefit along with the economy.
"Their current valuations are also attractive," said another dealer.
At 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index surged 19.60 points or 0.99 percent to 2,005.54. Turnover was an active 81.9 million shares with 172 gainers to 97 losers.

The foreign tranche of Singapore Press Holdings rose sharply to a new high of S$30.40 on its earnings prospects before easing to S$30.30. Volume was at 409,000 units including 241,000 married between $29.63-29.74.
Property-linked City Development and Cycle & Carriage as well as maritime Keppel Corp were among gainers.
"These are Singapore Inc companies. If the economy does well, they should as well," said the dealer with a local house.

Dealers said the electronic counters like Flextech Holdings and GP Batteries were underpinned by strong U.S. order books and buy recommendations on their earnings outlook. The SES electronics index was up at 127.69.
